title: OGEC Staff Advisory Opinion 15S-003: Acceptance of certain paid expenses for spouses of members of Board of Directors of Lane Transit District when attending various community events.

Dear Mr. Purdy:

This is in response to your correspondence received March 11, 2015 regarding how
Oregon Government Ethics law may apply to the acceptance of certain paid expenses
for the spouses of members of the Board of Directors of the Lane Transit District when
attending various community events.

OREGON GOVERNMENT ETHICS COMMISSION STAFF ADVISORY OPINION NO.
015S-003

STATED FACTS: Lane Transit District (LTD) is a mass transit special purpose district
organized under ORS Chapter 267. LTD is governed by a seven-member board of
directors, who are appointed by the Governor, The board of directors and staff of LTD
are active in the Eugene-Springfield and greater Lane County community. At certain
community events, organizations are given the option of purchasing individual tickets or
purchasing a table. If an entity elects to purchase a table, the price for the table is fixed,
regardless of how many individuals may attend the event and sit at the table. In the event
LTD purchases a table and is unable to fil all of those seats with board members or high-
level employees, LTD would like to make unused spots available to the spouses of board
members and other employees.

QUESTION 1: May LTD board members or employees accept from LTD paid expenses
for their spouses to attend various community events as described in the Stated facts?

ANSWER 1: No, with one exception. Public officials may not accept payment of
expenses from the government agency employer or the public body represented by the
public official for the attendance of their relatives at community events unless the
expenses are paid to the public official as part of an official compensation package.

Dwight G. Purdy

Commission Staff Advisory Opinion 15S-003
May 7, 2015

Page 2

ORS 244.040(1) prohibits a public official from using or attempting to use an official
position to obtain financial gain or to avoid financial detriment for the public official, a
relative of the public official or a business with which either are associated, if the
opportunity would not otherwise be available but for the public official’s holding the
position.

The stated facts appear to indicate that the opportunity for the spouses of board members
and other employees to attend various community events at the expense of LTD may be
an opportunity that would not otherwise be available but for the official positions held by
the board members and other employees.

While ORS 244.040(2)(a) allows public officials to accept any part of an official
compensation package as determined by the public body that the public official serves,
OAR 199-005-0035(3) prescribes the meaning of “official compensation package” as
used in ORS 244.040(2)(a). An “official compensation package” means the wages and
other benefits provided to the public official. To be part of the public official's “official
compensation package,” the wages and benefits must have been specifically approved
by the public body in a formal manner, such as through a union contract, an employment
contract, or other adopted personnel policies that apply generally to employees or other
public officials.

The stated facts appear to indicate that LTD would like to provide paid expenses for the
board members’ or employees’ spouses to attend various community events only in the
event that LTD purchases a table and is unable to fill all of the seats with board members
or high-level employees. In light of this prerequisite, it appears unlikely such a financial
benefit could be administered with the formality required by OAR 199-005-0035(3) and
ORS 244.040(2)(a).

QUESTION 2: Does the answer to QUESTION 1 depend upon the availability of board
members or certain high-level employees of LTD? In other words, must LTD offer a seat
at the purchased table to all board members and employees who may want to attend the
event in their official capacity before offering any available seat to board members’
Spouses or employees’ spouses?

ANSWER 2: No. The availability of board members or certain high-level employees has
no bearing on the prohibitions in ORS 244.040(1).

THIS RESPONSE ADDRESSES ONLY THE APPLICATION OF ORS 244 TO THE
FACTS STATED HEREIN. ANY RELEVANT INFORMATION, WHICH WAS NOT
INCLUDED BY THE REQUESTER OF THIS OPINION IN THE STATED FACTS,
COULD COMPLETELY CHANGE THE OUTCOME OF THIS OPINION. OTHER LAWS
OR REQUIREMENTS MAY ALSO APPLY. THIS IS NOT A FORMAL ADVISORY
OPINION PURSUANT TO ORS CHAPTER 244.280. THIS OPINION DOES NOT

ADDENDUM

RELEVANT STATUTES: The following Oregon Revised Statutes (ORS) are applicable
to the issues that are addressed in this Opinion:

244,020(14) “Public official” means any person who, when an alleged violation of
this chapter occurs, is serving the State of Oregon or any of its political
Subdivisions or any other public body as defined in ORS 174.109 as an elected
Official, appointed official, employee or agent, irrespective of whether the person
is compensated for the services.

244 .020(15) “Relative” means:

(a) The spouse, parent, stepparent, child, sibling, stepsibling, son-in-law or
daughter-in-law of the public official or candidate;

(b) The parent, stepparent, child, sibling, Stepsibling, son-in-law or
daughter-in-law of the spouse of the public official or candidate:

(c) Any individual for whom the public official or candidate has a legal
support obligation;

(d) Any individual for whom the public official provides benefits arising from
the public official’s public employment or from whom the public official
receives benefits arising from that individual's employment; or

244.040 Prohibited use of official position or office; exceptions; other
prohibited actions. (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, a
public official may not use or attempt to use official position or office to obtain
financial gain or avoidance of financial detriment for the public official, a relative or
member of the household of the public official, or any business with which the
public official or a relative or member of the household of the public official is
associated, if the financial gain or avoidance of financial detriment would not
otherwise be available but for the public official’s holding of the official position or
Office.

Dwight G. Purdy

Commission Staff Advisory Opinion 15S-003
May 7, 2015

Page 5

244.040(2) Subsection (1) of this section does not apply to:

(a) Any part of an official compensation package as determined by the
public body that the public official serves.

(b) The receipt by a public official or a relative or member of the household
of the public official of an honorarium or any other item allowed under ORS
244.042.

(c) Reimbursement of expenses.
(d) An unsolicited award for professional achievement.

(e) Gifts that do not exceed the limits specified in ORS 244.025 received by
a public official or a relative or member of the household of the public official
from a source that could reasonably be known to have a legislative or
administrative interest.

(f) Gifts received by a public official or a relative or member of the household
of the public official from a source that could not reasonably be known to
have a legislative or administrative interest.

(g) The receipt by a public official or a relative or member of the household
of the public official of any item, regardless of value, that is expressly
excluded from the definition of “gift” in ORS 244.020,

(h) Contributions made to a legal expense trust fund established under ORS
244.209 for the benefit of the public official,

The following Oregon Administrative Rules are applicable to the issues addressed herein:

199-005-0035(3) An “official compensation package” means the wages or other
benefits provided to the public official. To be part of the public official's ‘official
compensation package’, the wages and benefits must have been specifically
approved by the public body in a formal manner, such as through a union contract,
an employment contract, or other adopted personnel policies that apply generally
to employees or other public officials. ‘Official compensation package’ also
includes the direct payment of a public official's expenses by the public body, in
accordance with the public body’s policies,”
